affiliations: Texas Tech University School of Law

detail.title: The New Forever Rule For Record Retention

declarations.funderStatement: My salary.

detail.abstract:
In Murrin v. Commissioner the Third Circuit held that taxpayers cannot rely on the general three year period of limitations if anyone else is involved in preparing their tax return.  That is because §6501(c)(1) provides that “in the case of a false or fraudulent return with the intent to evade tax” the IRS has an unlimited time to assess.  Writes the Third Circuit: “the obvious construction of the statutory text is that the intent to evade tax must be present in a false or fraudulent return, irrespective of who possess that intent.” Thus, “whether a taxpayer, accountant, lawyer, or tax preparer evidenced such intent is beside the point.”  After Murrin, I must now advise taxpayers to keep their records forever, if anyone other than the taxpayer has participated in the preparation of the return. 

This article explains how Murrin has changed the law and why it means taxpayers can no longer predict if and when the IRS will audit a return they have filed with help from a third party.  They must keep their records....forever.

title: TikTok Triage, Disclaimers, and the Reasonable Follower: A Unified Framework for Medical Influencer Liability
affiliations: and

detail.title: TikTok Triage, Disclaimers, and the Reasonable Follower: A Unified Framework for Medical Influencer Liability

declarations.declarationOfInterest: None.
declarations.funderStatement: None.

detail.abstract: Credentialed healthcare influencers on social media often provide services functionally indistinguishable from clinical care. Yet they escape malpractice liability because no formal physician-patient relationship was ever established. This Article argues that current doctrine errs in permitting this outcome. Fowler, Helveston, and Robinson's landmark Influencer Speech-Torts framework establishes that health influencers can face negligence liability, but it operates in general negligence rather than medical malpractice, leaving the physician-patient relationship formation question unaddressed. Nor does it analyze the interactive engagement tier of comment replies, direct messages, monetized livestreams, and paid subscriber communities as a distinct doctrinal problem. This Article fills these gaps and extends the framework to cover two further questions: whether the "not medical advice" disclaimer defeats liability, and how courts should assess foreseeability of reliance harm in the broadcast tier where most health influencing occurs. Drawing on the foreseeability standard of Warren v. Dinter, the undertaking doctrine of Restatement (Second) of Torts § 323, and the Physician Payments Sunshine Act, this Article proposes three doctrinal tools: the undertaking-by-interaction standard, the reliance-limitation test, and the reasonable follower standard. Parasocial relationship theory and the positive law of telemedicine supply the supporting framework. Together, these tools address the full spectrum of medical influencer liability, from interactive malpractice to broadcast negligence.

title: Equilibrium Existence in Wolinsky (1986)
affiliations: Shandong University

detail.title: Equilibrium Existence in Wolinsky (1986)
detail.abstract: This paper revisits the consumer search and price competition model of Wolinsky (1986). Suppose that the market has a finite number of firms, match values between firms and consumers have log-concave densities, the reservation match value lies in the interior of the support, and the outside option is sufficiently low to induce active search. This paper proves that there is a unique symmetric equilibrium in pure strategies.

title: State AI Governance under Constitutional Constraint: An Architecture for Deployer-centered, Process-based AI Accountability Designed to Survive Dormant Commerce Clause and Preemption Scrutiny

detail.title: State AI Governance under Constitutional Constraint: An Architecture for Deployer-centered, Process-based AI Accountability Designed to Survive Dormant Commerce Clause and Preemption Scrutiny

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing personal or financial interests. AI-use disclosure: Artificial intelligence tools were used to support the research for this Article: locating and retrieving primary legal sources, organizing and verifying the evidence base, and assisting with drafting and formatting. The ideas, analytical framework, arguments, insights, and conclusions are the original work of the author. AI-assisted output, including cited authorities and quotations, was reviewed and verified against primary sources before use under the author's direction. Generative AI output may contain unintended errors. A fuller note on method appears in the Article's front matter.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
Federal AI policy has remade itself three times in twenty-six months. An executive order built on safety commitments gave way to one built on removing them; a preemption-minded successor now directs the Justice Department to litigate against state AI statutes while conceding, in its own carve-outs, that whole domains of state authority will remain. States told to wait for stable federal ground are waiting for ground that is not coming.
This Article argues that the constitutional doctrines usually framed as obstacles to state AI regulation, the dormant Commerce Clause and federal preemption, are better understood as design inputs that select a particular regulatory architecture. States should not regulate AI as a technology category. They should regulate the AI-mediated decision environments inside domains they already control (employment, housing, insurance, healthcare, education, public benefits, criminal justice) by imposing process-based obligations on deployers and anchoring those obligations in authorities the federal political branches have not displaced and could not displace in one stroke without unraveling multiple foundational federal-state settlements: consumer protection, civil rights enforcement, sector licensing, and public procurement.
The Article makes three contributions. First, a constitutional design move: it derives the deployer-centered architecture from the doctrine itself, showing why model-centric statutes draw extraterritoriality and obstacle-preemption fire that decision-environment statutes largely avoid. Second, a concept: regulatory resilience, durability achieved through enduring authorities rather than preemption-proofing. Third, a translation: it translates the NIST AI Risk Management Framework and ISO/IEC 42001 from voluntary management constructs into legally cognizable deployer duties, with worked statutory text for four governance primitives (procurement-first controls, deployer-centered impact assessments, audit-trail mandates, and dispute-and-remedy pathways) and worked sector applications for hospital AI, hiring AI, and insurance underwriting AI.

title: An Explainable Machine Learning Analysis of Retail Renewable Premiums
affiliations: Ohio State University (OSU), Ohio State University (OSU), John Glenn College of Public Affairs, Ohio State University (OSU), Ohio State University (OSU), Exeter Associates, Lehigh University and Lehigh University

detail.title: An Explainable Machine Learning Analysis of Retail Renewable Premiums
detail.abstract: Estimating the supplier's margin on retail renewable energy is persistently challenging. 14 U.S. states and several international jurisdictions have implemented retail restructuring (i.e., 'retail choice') through which consumers can shop for electricity supply from marketers. These marketers often offer plans with varying compositions of renewable energy supplied by renewable energy certificates (RECs). This study quantifies the renewable energy margin on residential electricity offers using comprehensive data from Ohio's retail choice market (2014-2023). We develop an algorithm that matches renewable and non-renewable offers by the same supplier on the same day, with virtually identical offer details (e.g., maturity, monthly fee, termination fee) over 120,000 matched contracts. Using a gradient boosting model with SHAP (Shapley Additive Explanations), we estimate the influence of contract features and wholesale market conditions (e.g., forward hub prices) on the renewable energy margin of renewable offers. On average, renewable contracts include a markup of 7.67% (price difference of 0.642 cents/kWh). However, results also indicate that longer contract maturities and higher early termination fees are associated with lower renewable energy premiums, suggesting that renewable premiums vary systematically across contract structures. Importantly, we find robust empirical evidence for the presence of a trigger price: when forward wholesale energy prices are below $47.9/MWh, marketers obtain renewable energy premiums through higher marginal prices. Above this trigger, marketers no longer obtain a higher premium on renewable offers and instead manipulate maturities and early termination fees. Policy implications for market design and societal environmental objectives are presented.

title: Execution-Verified Scientific Reasoning for Autonomous Finite-Element Solver Synthesis with Domain-Adapted Large Language Models
affiliations: and University of Maryland at Baltimore County

detail.title: Execution-Verified Scientific Reasoning for Autonomous Finite-Element Solver Synthesis with Domain-Adapted Large Language Models
detail.abstract: Partial differential equation (PDE)-based simulation is central to engineering analysis and design, yet constructing reliable finite element method (FEM) solvers from high-level physical descriptions remains labor intensive. This workflow requires physical interpretation, governing-equation formulation, weak-form derivation, numerical discretization, implementation, and runtime validation; an error at any stage can produce code that appears plausible but represents an incorrect or non-executable model. This paper presents an execution-verified framework for autonomous PDE-to-FEM solver synthesis using domain-adapted large language models (LLMs). The framework formulates solver synthesis as a structured reasoning process linking physical-semantic parsing, operator-level PDE assembly, boundary and initialcondition specification, variational formulation, finite-element discretization, executable FEniCSx/Gmsh code generation, and runtime verification. An execution-verified synthetic data factory generates reasoningto-code trajectories and a physics-aware correction corpus, enabling a compact 2-billion-parameter opensource model to learn relationships among physical assumptions, numerical formulation, solver implementation, and execution outcome. Evaluation on 75 unseen PDE problems across canonical, intermediate, and complex tiers shows that the adapted model achieves 100.0%, 93.3%, and 60.0% execution success, respectively, and obtains the strongest weighted ReasoningScore, SpecScore, execution rate, and RuntimeQualityScore among all baselines under a single-pass, no-repair protocol. These results show that reliable AI-assisted physics-based simulation depends not only on model scale, but also on structured domain supervision and execution-based validation. This work contributes a structured, execution-verified reasoning-supervision method for LLMs, applied here to automate FEM solver generation for PDE-based engineering simulations.

title: Bridges and Gaps: Operationalizing EU-CPTPP Cooperation

detail.title: Bridges and Gaps: Operationalizing EU-CPTPP Cooperation
detail.abstract: This note explores how the 39 members of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) and the European Union (EU) can move towards a more structured relationship given their mutual interests in preserving rules-based trade as "middle powers" in geopolitical terms and as "small open economies" in economic terms, at a time of "rupture" in the international political and economic system. The note is premised on four propositions. measures such as cumulation in rules of origin to promote a deepening of mutual trade on a WTO-consistent basis. • Fourth, use the review of the CPTPP digital economy chapter to fill the gap in the WTO framework for the digital economy; this will involve parsing "electronic transmissions" into GATT-governed digital products that are "like" goods; GATS-governed digital products that are "like" services; and data, whose value is explicitly captured in trade accounts and reflected in estimated trade balances, with measures that enable sovereignty in governance of the digital economy. Ultimately, the EU-CPTPP "bridge" can promote the development of a market with the scale to compete with China and the United States while retaining the perspectives and values of small open economies.

title: The Variance Risk Premium: Model-Free Measurement, Term Structure, and the Economics of Selling Volatility

detail.title: The Variance Risk Premium: Model-Free Measurement, Term Structure, and the Economics of Selling Volatility
detail.abstract: Option-implied variance on the S&P 500 tends to run higher than the variance that ends up realized. In this paper, we derive the model-free measurement apparatus underlying that fact from first principles. The derivation starts with log-contract replication of realized variance via Itô's lemma. We then prove the Carr-Madan spanning identity. Finally, we build the exact discretization bridge to the CBOE's VIX formula. We then measure the resulting variance risk premium over 22 years of daily S&P 500 and VIX data (2004-2026). To do this, we use a forward-window realized-variance convention argued to be the only construction consistent with the premium's economic meaning. The premium averages approximately 3.5 volatility points. It is positive on 84% of sample days, and has a left-skewed distribution (skewness-7 in variance units). Additionally, its sign inverts during the global financial crisis, though not in every crisis regime in the sample. A VIX futures term structure built over 2007-2026 shows contango on 82% of days. It mirrors the same premium from a second instrument. A short-volatility strategy constructed from that curve illustrates the premium's economic payoff profile which is steady accumulated gains punctuated by catastrophic single-day losses. Section 6 relates these findings to a companion paper on rough volatility. It draws the line between what path roughness explains about this premium and what it leaves untouched.

title: Is Botswana Working for All Batswana? From Industrial Development to Inclusive Participation in a Changing Economy
affiliations: Regional Integration & Trade Governance Professional

detail.title: Is Botswana Working for All Batswana? From Industrial Development to Inclusive Participation in a Changing Economy
detail.abstract: For six decades, the Republic of Botswana has stood as an exemplary paradigm of African development, transitioning from one of the poorest protectorates in 1966 to an upper-middle-income country. This trajectory was constructed upon a highly institutionalized developmental state model, prudent mineral rent management, macroeconomic stability, and substantial social investments. However, as the nation enters its seventh decade, this mineral-dependent, capital-intensive growth model has reached its structural limits. Despite the high gross domestic product (GDP) per capita, structural inequalities remain deeply entrenched. Women, youth and persons with disabilities (PWDs) continue to face systemic exclusion and uneven integration into Botswana's socioeconomic and political architecture. This paper presents a systematic policy coherence audit of Botswana's major developmental strategies, demonstrating that existing policy instruments have generated transactional programmes rather than transformative participation. With the contemporary structural decline in global diamond markets acting as an economic accelerant of inequality, Botswana faces an urgent structural crossroads. The paper argues that the convergence of domestic policy reform and emerging continental frameworks, particularly the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA) presents a historic opportunity to shift from growth-centered to inclusive development. To operationalize this transition, we introduce an Inclusive Industrial Transformation Framework (IITF) designed to move beyond distributive welfare toward a capability-enhancing, co-creative economy that guarantees sustainable, democratic participation for all Batswana by 2066.

title: On the Macroeconomic Dynamics of the Circular Economy: A Stock-Flow Consistent Model
affiliations: and Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile

detail.title: On the Macroeconomic Dynamics of the Circular Economy: A Stock-Flow Consistent Model
detail.abstract: This paper develops a dynamic ecological-macroeconomic model of the circular economy that integrates the core strategies of reducing, reusing, and recycling within a unified intertemporal framework. The model treats produced capital, available material stocks, waste liabilities, and dissipated residuals as physically interconnected stocks subject to material-balance constraints. Its central contribution is to show how capital depreciation, when interpreted as deferred residual generation rather than only as a loss of productive services, changes the optimal growth problem. Two macroeconomic mechanisms emerge from the analysis: a circular capital discount, reflecting the shadow cost of future residuals embodied in current investment, and a wasteliability drag, through which depreciation-related and production-related residuals lower the effective intertemporal return to capital and reduce sustainable consumption relative to a linear benchmark. We show analytically that these mechanisms imply a liability-adjusted golden rule of capital accumulation and a lower socially optimal steady-state capital stock than in the standard neoclassical model. The paper also maps the planner's allocation into a decentralized system of circular Pigouvian incentives, derives a circularly adjusted accounting identity for comprehensive wealth, and provides calibrated transition exercises showing how Reduce, Reuse, and Recycle operate through distinct macroeconomic channels. The results suggest that circular strategies reshape growth not by eliminating intertemporal trade-offs, but by changing the shadow valuation of capital accumulation, residual generation, and material recovery.

title: Performance Is Not Value Creation: A Capital-Aware Framework for Evaluating Hedge Fund Managers
affiliations: Pernas Research

detail.title: Performance Is Not Value Creation: A Capital-Aware Framework for Evaluating Hedge Fund Managers
detail.abstract:
The hedge fund industry primarily evaluates managers using capital-agnostic performance measures such as annualized return, alpha, Sharpe ratio, and related return statistics. While these measures remain useful for evaluating investment performance, they are not designed to measure a different and arguably more economically important concept: benchmark-adjusted wealth creation on the capital investors actually entrusted to a manager. As managers attract more capital over time, strong early returns earned on a small asset base can continue to dominate the track record even if much larger pools of capital later receive mediocre or benchmark-lagging results.

This paper argues that investment performance and economic value creation are distinct concepts, and that both should be measured. To address this measurement gap, it introduces Excess Wealth Added (EWA), a capital-aware measure of cumulative benchmark-adjusted wealth creation, and Excess Wealth Efficiency (EWE), a complementary asset-weighted measure of value creation efficiency relative to the capital entrusted to the manager.

The purpose of EWA and EWE is not to replace traditional performance statistics, but to complement them by measuring something they were never intended to measure: the economic value created for investors. Together, these measures provide a broader framework for evaluating active managers based not only on how well they performed, but on how much benchmark-adjusted wealth they created and how efficiently they created it relative to the capital entrusted to them.

title: National Determinants of Coffee Prices in Italy: An Econometric Analysis

detail.title: National Determinants of Coffee Prices in Italy: An Econometric Analysis

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this study, as it relies exclusively on secondary data and does not involve human participants.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract: Coffee is one of the most widespread and culturally significant consumer goods in Italy: the domestic market is currently worth around €5.2 billion, with per capita consumption of approximately 5.5 kg per year. This paper analyses the determinants of coffee consumer prices in Italy over the period 2013-2025, using a monthly dataset constructed by integrating Eurostat, ECB, World Bank and national sources. The estimated multiple OLS regression model includes both national variables energy costs, general inflation, interest rates and labour costs and international variables oil prices and the euro/dollar exchange rate with the discussion of results focused on national determinants. Complementing the analysis with a multicollinearity test (VIF), an endogeneity test using instrumental variables, and the Hausman test, the study shows that electricity prices and the interest rate are the most robust determinants of coffee prices in Italy. The analysis is completed by an ARIMA-GARCH model of the Italian coffee price time series, which reveals a significant seasonal structure and high volatility persistence (α+β ≈ 0.95). The results provide useful insights for understanding the domestic transmission of inflationary pressures on coffee prices and for assessing the adaptation strategies of households and the national supply chain.

title: Business, Commodity, And Financial Cycles in Nigeria: The Role of Macroeconomic Policy
affiliations: Central Bank of Nigeria

detail.title: Business, Commodity, And Financial Cycles in Nigeria: The Role of Macroeconomic Policy
detail.abstract: The paper examines the role of macroeconomic policy in stabilising the fluctuations generated by the simultaneous interactions between business, commodity and financial cycles in a small open resource-rich economy. The results reveal that both fiscal and monetary policy are important stabilising tools for the economic cycles. However, both policies counteract each other, resulting in an overall neutral policy stance. The results further show that the policy instruments have weak influence on the commodity cycle. These findings imply that even though the policy instruments are important in stabilising the economy, achieving the appropriate policy mix is equally important, and that macroeconomic policy alone may be insufficient to stabilise the shocks from commodity price fluctuations. By examining the impact of fiscal and monetary policy on business, commodity, and financial cycles in Nigeria, the study contributes to the understanding the role of macroeconomic policy in economic stabilisation in resource-rich developing countries.

title: Strong Alignment and Contract Form in Robust Teams Linear Sharing under Risk Neutrality and Utility-Affine Contracts under Risk Aversion
affiliations: The University of Sydney

detail.title: Strong Alignment and Contract Form in Robust Teams Linear Sharing under Risk Neutrality and Utility-Affine Contracts under Risk Aversion
detail.abstract: This note connects two ingredients in robust team moral hazard that are individually insufficient to determine contract form. Primal-dual analysis yields a weighted aggregate identity for the agents' compensation schedules, but that identity admits many nonlinear contracts. Alignment restricts the agents to rank distributions of aggregate performance in the same direction, but alignment alone permits a nonlinear common incentive index. We distinguish the strict-to-weak condition of Dai and Toikka [2022], called Dai-Toikka alignment, from a weak-to-weak condition, called strong alignment. On a convex and Dirac-rich distribution domain, strong alignment makes every nonconstant compensation schedule a positive affine transformation of any other in the payoff space relevant to the agents. For risk-neutral agents, this is wage space; combining the resulting wage-affine property with the aggregate identity and two-sided limited liability proves that every full-contact optimum is a vector of positive linear sharing contracts. For risk-averse agents, alignment must instead be imposed on expected Bernoulli utility from compensation. It then implies that the gross utility schedules u i • w i are positive affine transformations of one another. The risk-averse aggregate dual identity determines a common utility index and generally produces nonlinear monetary wages. Risk neutrality is recovered as the special case in which this index and all wages are linear. We also recover the closed-form robust team shares in a separable risk-neutral environment. An appendix extends the structural argument to multi-member supply-chain contracts and states its risk-averse counterpart.

title: Do Litter Cleanups Benefit Wildlife? Evidence from U.S. Birds
affiliations: University of Illinois, Urbana-Champaign and Old Dominion University - Economics

detail.title: Do Litter Cleanups Benefit Wildlife? Evidence from U.S. Birds

declarations.declarationOfInterest: We declare that we have no relevant or material financial interests that relate to the research described in this paper. This project received no external financial support. No party had the right to review the paper prior to circulation.

detail.abstract: Improperly discarded litter poses ecological risks, yet little evidence documents whether cleanup activities generate measurable environmental benefits. We provide the first causal estimates of the effects of nonprofit litter cleanup events on bird abundance in the United States. We combine cleanup-event-level data from the Ocean Conservancy's International Coastal Cleanup program with county-level abundance indices derived from eBird from 2015-2022 and estimate staggered-adoption event-study models using both two-way fixed effects and bias-corrected estimators. Cleanup events increase bird abundance by 0.026 index points, or 0.67 percent of the county mean, with effects that accumulate over three years and persist. Cleanup activity does not affect birder effort, indicating the results are not driven by changes in bird detection. Heterogeneity analyses show that landbirds and non-scavenger species drive the positive average effects, whereas scavenger species that feed on litter decrease in abundance after litter removal. Given the modest cost of volunteer cleanups and their broader ecological benefits, these findings highlight that litter removal efforts can serve as a cost-effective tool for improving bird abundance.

title: Exposing the Value of Receiving and Giving Help across 12 European Countries: a Longitudinal Analysis of Self-Perceived Health

detail.title: Exposing the Value of Receiving and Giving Help across 12 European Countries: a Longitudinal Analysis of Self-Perceived Health
detail.abstract: The act of receiving and giving help is commonly expected to improve older people's health. In this article, this expectation is explored through a longitudinal analysis of a representative sample of 29,995 respondents aged 59 to 89 in 2011 from 12 European countries documented in the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE) for the period 2011 to 2022. An unordered correlated random-effects (CRE), an ordered fixed-effects logistic (FEO), as well as an ordered random-effects logistic panel estimator (REO), all with longitudinal calibrated weights, are used to estimate the relationship between self-perceived health, receiving, and giving help. Additionally, a stereotype ordered logistic estimator (SO) is included to support the detected interaction effect between receiving and giving help. Overall, the study documents the positive impact on self-reported health status of income, doing activities and being satisfied with life, as well as the negative impact of age and having limitations. The Danish older people report the best health status, followed by the Swedes and the Swiss. Moreover, the study highlights that receiving help relates to worse self-perceived health, and that giving help relates to better self-perceived health. Above all, the study reveals the potential of the act of giving help to improve the self-perceived health status, in particular of those who receive help.

title: Are Pensions and Disability Benefits concordant with Means and Health? A Tobit Approach to SHARE data from 50-to-89-year-olds covering 12 European Countries from 2015 to 2022

detail.title: Are Pensions and Disability Benefits concordant with Means and Health? A Tobit Approach to SHARE data from 50-to-89-year-olds covering 12 European Countries from 2015 to 2022
detail.abstract: Public pensions and benefits are a cornerstone for safeguarding citizens' standard of living. This study focuses on the determinants of old-age pensions as well as disability pensions and benefits. The data is provided by the Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE), and covers people aged 50 to 89 years old for the period 2015 to 2022 in 12 European countries. The relationship between the determinants and old-age as well as disability pensions is estimated using Multi-effects and Random-Effects Tobit estimators with a minimum of 106,240 observations of minimum 47,832 respondents. The results indicate that both old-age and disability pensions appear to be limited complementary across countries. Old-age pensions are lower at lower self-reported health levels, while disability pensions and benefits appear to be higher. Moreover, the public payment schemes appear to account for the remaining available income of the beneficiary, implying that a given fairness is incorporated in the payment policies. Remarkably, both payments reveal the presence of a pension gender gap, potentially arising from a preceding wage gap. Overall, the study illustrates on a high level the fair allocation of available means to old-age as well as disability pensions across a substantial part of Europe.

title: Financial Distress and Homeownership: Evidence from SHARE Data covering 50-to 90-year-old Citizens of the Nordic and Baltic States from 2020 to 2022

detail.title: Financial Distress and Homeownership: Evidence from SHARE Data covering 50-to 90-year-old Citizens of the Nordic and Baltic States from 2020 to 2022
detail.abstract: Homeownership is a societal and financial stronghold for people across the world. However, achieving or sustaining homeownership may come with a given cost. This study focuses on financial distress in relation to homeownership and other relevant factors like health. It relies on data from the Survey of Health, Ageing, and Retirement in Europe (SHARE) for citizens of the Nordic and Baltic States aged 50 to 90 years old. The analysis is completed with a logistic (N = 2,878) and ordered logistic (N = 7,030) estimator, which both model the change in the regressed variables from 2020 to 2022. The main findings reveal that homeownership exit alone does not relieve financial distress, yet results in an improvement in combination with a budget-for-food and income improvement. In contrast, a liabilities relief and a change in job situation appear to hinder a financial distress improvement. Overall, the findings can be regarded as relevant for policymakers' quest for appropriate governmental action to handle citizens' difficulties with making end meets which arise from sustaining homeownership.
